summary: Conditional deprovisioning: shared service account tokens + remote laptop located at partner office
description:
Issue summary: Temporary researcher (external contractor) completed assignment yesterday but HR flagged a partial offboarding request because: 1) contractor appears in SCIM with two different email variants (username vs corporate email), 2) they had write access to a shared CI service account, and 3) their assigned company laptop is physically located at a partner site in eu-west.

Impact: If we perform a full automated deprovision (SCIM-based removal) we risk breaking the shared CI service account or losing audit continuity for in-flight builds. If we delay deprovision, the contractor retains access longer than policy allows and the asset stays uncollected. HR requests guidance and operational execution to: revoke personal access where safe, rotate shared account tokens, and arrange secure recovery or remote wipe of device.

Environment: Production identity provider sync (SCIM) to Okta, SSO enabled across GitHub org and internal Confluence, asset inventory in AssetDB, device management via Jamf and partner office custody records.

Expected: Clear stepwise offboarding that preserves service continuity for shared accounts while ensuring access removal and asset retrieval per offboarding policy.

Actual: Conflicting SCIM attributes and shared-sa usage prevents straightforward automated removal. Asset location is offsite under partner custody requiring logistics coordination.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Query SCIM user record for contractor 't.researcher' in Okta -> shows primaryEmail t.researcher@contractor.example and altUsername tresearcher; 2) Check GitHub org membership -> user still in org with PR approvals and access to 'infra/ci' protected repo; 3) Check AssetDB -> device tag RW-2025-408 marked at partner:eu-west-site-B with custody note 'partner-storage-2025-11'.
logs:
SCIM export snippet: primaryEmail=t.researcher@contractor.example; altUsername=tresearcher; active=true
GitHub audit: user tresearcher approved 3 PRs in infra/ci in last 7 days, token created 2026-02-28 for shared-sa 'ci-build@redwood-infra' shows last used 2026-03-08
AssetDB: RW-2025-408 last scanned 2026-02-25 at partner eu-west-site-B (scan id: SCAN-88412)
comments: 2026-03-09 09:12: Evelyn Chen (HR): Received offboarding request for contract id 2025-TR. Policy says immediate SSO disable but asks to preserve CI pipeline continuity until replacement vetted. Can Support propose a safe sequence?
2026-03-09 10:05: Marco Alvarez (IAM): I'll investigate SCIM record and shared SA usage. Will avoid removing the user until we rotate shared tokens. Assigning device recovery to device-ops.

2026-03-09 11:40: Priya Rao (Device-ops): Partner confirms device present and flagged for pickup next available courier window. Need confirmation on whether to perform remote wipe or return to partner for handoff.

2026-03-09 14:30: Jamal Khan (SRE): Found that 'ci-build@redwood-infra' has two active PATs and one machine user token linked to the contractor. Recommend rotating tokens and adding short-lived deploy keys before removing user.
2026-03-10 08:22: Marco Alvarez: Created temporary plan (see investigation notes). Waiting on HR to approve token rotation window and for partner to confirm pick-up ETA.
investigation_notes: SCIM mapping issue: provisioning uses 'username' attribute for legacy contractors while our deprovisioning script expects 'primaryEmail'. This caused duplicate entries and prevented the automated offboard job from matching the correct identity.

Shared SA risk: contractor's personal GH account was used to create a machine token for 'ci-build@redwood-infra' on 2026-02-28. Two active PATs still exist; one has last activity 2026-03-08. No recent CI failures observed, but token owners include contractor and one service runner.

Asset custody: partner asset log indicates RW-2025-408 under partner custody with locked storage. Partner will allow courier pickup on business days; requires asset tag and signed chain-of-custody form (template linked).

Policy ambiguity: Offboarding runbook currently instructs immediate SSO disable for contractors. It lacks guidance for conditional deprovisioning when contractor-owned credentials are attached to shared service accounts.
resolution:
Workaround implemented 2026-03-11: 1) Disabled contractor's direct SSO access to internal Console and Slack accounts to block interactive sessions. 2) Rotated tokens for 'ci-build@redwood-infra' and invalidated contractor-linked PATs; created short-lived deploy key for the CI runner to preserve pipeline continuity. 3) Notified partner to schedule courier pickup; device-ops to perform remote wipe on receipt if requested. 4) Logged actions in offboarding audit (CONFLUENCE: /display/Ops/Offboarding-Audit-2026-03-11).

Follow-ups (owners): Marco Alvarez to file a small SCIM mapping change PR to prefer primaryEmail for contractor deprovisions (related PR: GH-PR-1289). Priya Rao to confirm pickup and update AssetDB entry. HR (Evelyn Chen) to approve updated runbook language clarifying conditional deprovisioning for shared SAs. Target to close all follow-ups by 2026-03-18.
